scope: Twelve acquired EAAI research-article full texts; all judgments are based on complete-PDF reading.
strength_rule: S-High requires occurrence in at least five papers and at least 70% of the comparable subset. Lower-frequency patterns are S-Medium or O/Low and are not treated as journal requirements.

papers.title: Deep reinforcement learning for periodic Unmanned Aerial Vehicle task allocation and path planning with a Fixed Nest Station in power inspection
papers.introduction_move: Engineering inspection requirements → three combinatorial challenges → mechanism-to-problem contributions.
papers.methods_granularity: Graph/MILP and MDP before pruning, attention actor–critic, reward and algorithm; notation, pseudocode and parameters supplied.
papers.results_logic: Training → exact small-scale verification → large-scale multi-metric comparison → ablation → sensitivity.
papers.discussion_boundary: Trade-offs are visible, but some feasibility/generalisation wording exceeds the evidence and is excluded from the model style.
papers.figure_role: Scenario/formulation, architecture, training, metrics, distributions, trade-off, ablation and route evidence form a sequential argument.
papers.citation_function: Mechanism-organised review; citations locate exact scheduling, topology and DRL gaps.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Ten independent runs and solver status support bounded comparisons; no universal deployment claim.
papers.noncopy: Periodic-frequency model, 28-day horizon, MILP/DSP/TAA equations, FE indicator, parameters, results, wording and reference combination.

papers.title: Asynchronous multithreading reinforcement learning with attention-based significance measurement for collision-free robot navigation
papers.introduction_move: Safety need → navigation-method taxonomy and comparison table → deficiencies → contributions.
papers.methods_granularity: POMDP and executable control precede system, observation/action/reward, replay significance, attention and PPO training.
papers.results_logic: Ablations/configurations → sensitivity → unseen scenarios → stress/scaling → physical validation.
papers.discussion_boundary: Simulation and real-robot evidence are separated; local failure limits are reported, while unsupported superlatives are not imitated.
papers.figure_role: Configuration tables define interventions; progressively harder tests and runtime decomposition support engineering claims.
papers.citation_function: Taxonomy and comparison table connect prior mechanisms to explicit limitations.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Sample counts and metric denominators are stated; physical claims remain limited to the disclosed platform and protocol.
papers.noncopy: ASMAC/SMRR/LAM, reward, asynchronous workers, sensor/control details, scenarios, metrics, runtime and physical-validation rhetoric.

papers.title: Situation-aware deep reinforcement learning for unmanned aerial vehicle swarm navigation in dynamic multi-obstacle environments
papers.introduction_move: Dynamic swarm task → method taxonomy → three deficiencies → module-level contributions.
papers.methods_granularity: Notation and component sections culminate in integrated data flow, pseudocode, reward, uncertainty and convergence discussion.
papers.results_logic: Protocol roadmap → weights/filter/training comparisons → statistics → ablation → scaling → extreme conditions → synthesis.
papers.discussion_boundary: Significance and effect size are paired; important non-significant and adverse training-cost outcomes remain visible.
papers.figure_role: Plots and synthesis tables connect training, robustness, scaling and component evidence.
papers.citation_function: References are grouped by the exact sensing, optimisation and learning deficiencies addressed.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Monte Carlo means/SD, effect sizes and named perturbations support qualified robustness claims, not causal proof of every module.
papers.noncopy: AHF/SAPO/CNN-LSTM/DDPG, reward and uncertainty models, parameters, convergence language, results and references.

papers.title: Evaluating reinforcement learning-based neural controllers for quadcopter navigation in windy conditions
papers.introduction_move: Wind-disturbed waypoint problem → gap in training design/state representation → evaluated factors and contributions.
papers.methods_granularity: MDP/PPO/SHAP preliminaries precede task, variants, simulator, baselines, protocol and operational metrics.
papers.results_logic: Classical baseline → training-condition variants → state variants → cautious feature attribution; disaggregated routes in appendix.
papers.discussion_boundary: Neutral/detrimental variants and nominal-versus-robustness costs are retained; simulation-to-real boundary is explicit.
papers.figure_role: Aggregate main plots establish conclusions; trajectory-specific appendix evidence explains heterogeneity.
papers.citation_function: Related work is split by control, wind robustness and explainability functions.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Training seeds and repeated rollouts support evaluation claims; SHAP observations are not causal explanations.
papers.noncopy: AirSim wind model, trajectories, controller parameters, SHAP, state variables, tolerances, results and physical-system suggestions.

papers.title: Human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning for dynamic soaring: A trajectory planning and control integrated system
papers.introduction_move: Motivation and physical challenge → optimal-control limitations → integrated HITL contribution.
papers.methods_granularity: Reference optimiser and environment fidelity precede the human–DRL loop, SAC, phase reward, criteria and network.
papers.results_logic: Reference → HITL comparison → state/action traces → wind/initialisation perturbations → dedicated limitations.
papers.discussion_boundary: Adverse time, footprint, sensitivity and training cost are reported; convergence, transfer and flight limits are explicit.
papers.figure_role: 3D routes, projections and state/action histories jointly expose feasibility and failure sensitivity.
papers.citation_function: Problem-specific optimal-control, RL and HITL evidence constructs the gap without supplying a transferable reference set.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Perturbation-specific observations support simulation feasibility only; no real-flight readiness claim.
papers.noncopy: Dynamic-soaring formulation, GPOPS/SNOPT, SAC/HITL loop, rewards, aerodynamics, thresholds, findings and references.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning based multi-perspective motion planning of manned electric vertical take-off and landing vehicle in urban environment with wind fields
papers.introduction_move: Aircraft/passenger/city perspectives → multi-objective coverage gap → five mapped contributions.
papers.methods_granularity: POMDP, action/observation/reward and external energy/noise/wind models precede PPO and experiment protocol.
papers.results_logic: Implementation comparison → per-objective algorithm results → joint objective → component-removal ablation → limitations.
papers.discussion_boundary: Physical-model simplifications, training burden, scalarisation costs and individual comparator wins are preserved.
papers.figure_role: Coverage tables make novelty auditable; result/ablation tables link objectives, failures and costs.
papers.citation_function: Algorithm- and objective-coverage tables assign references to specific missing engineering dimensions.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Named wind cases support scenario-bounded comparison; complex objectives are not declared globally optimal.
papers.noncopy: eVTOL/Atlanta/CFD, passenger/acoustic models, modified PPO, rewards, weights, results and references.

papers.title: Path planning via reinforcement learning with closed-loop motion control and field tests
papers.introduction_move: Dynamic feasibility and real-time requirement → layered architecture gap → planner/controller/field contributions.
papers.methods_granularity: One-step RL and path representation are followed by complete vehicle, instrumentation and MPC sections.
papers.results_logic: Algorithm × representation → randomisation → simulation comparator → controlled field tests.
papers.discussion_boundary: Planning/control latencies and simulation/field roles are separated; impossible scenarios and hierarchy drawbacks remain explicit.
papers.figure_role: Training, domain shifts, execution error and field evidence support separate planning and control claims.
papers.citation_function: Search, optimisation, RL and MPC references locate the real-time feasibility gap.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Field claims are limited to disclosed runs/hardware; domain-randomised training is not treated as universal transfer.
papers.noncopy: ISO manoeuvre, TD3/MPC, polynomial path, vehicle models/hardware, timing, randomisation and field-test claims.

papers.title: Layered learning in a quadrotor drone: Simultaneous controlling and path planning using optimal fuzzy fractional order proportional integral derivative and proximal policy optimization
papers.methods_granularity: Dynamics and lower-level controller optimisation precede PPO state/action/reward and manoeuvre constraints.
papers.results_logic: Controller responses → PPO/network results → test stand → disturbances → qualitative loop flight.
papers.discussion_boundary: Simulation dependence, lab mismatch and local optima are stated; qualitative flight evidence is not a quantitative validation model.
papers.figure_role: Physical response metrics and hardware tables support controller claims; high-level flight evidence remains largely qualitative.
papers.citation_function: Broad control/optimisation/DRL survey supports the layered architecture rationale.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: No replicated uncertainty reporting; therefore its practices cannot establish a high-strength journal convention.
papers.noncopy: Fuzzy/FOPID/GA/PSO/Taguchi, dynamics, rewards, network, hardware, qualitative flight claims and references.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning based robot navigation using illegal actions for autonomous docking of surface vehicles in unknown environments
papers.introduction_move: Safety-critical docking gap → perception-to-action RL, mask mechanism and tiered validation contributions.
papers.methods_granularity: A2C/PPO precede navigation states/actions/rewards and the training-only illegal-action mask.
papers.results_logic: Mask variants → learning behaviour → robustness/unseen layouts → A* quality–time comparison → two physical tiers.
papers.discussion_boundary: Training-only masking is separated from testing; comparator advantages, failures and physical-tier limits are reported.
papers.figure_role: Curves, event diagnostics, route quality, processing time and action traces explain distinct aspects of behaviour.
papers.citation_function: Prior work is organised by route tracking, high-level decisions, simulation-only limitations and deployment loss.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Ten training instances and repeated scenario episodes support bounded mask and robustness claims, not independent effects of all internal rules.
papers.noncopy: Docking states/actions, illegal-action windows, reward, curriculum, sea conditions, A* settings, hardware and physical results.

papers.title: A reliable traversability learning method based on human-demonstrated risk cost mapping for mobile robots over uneven terrain
papers.introduction_move: Manual terrain rewards as bottleneck → learned risk preference → feature/IRL/planning contributions.
papers.methods_granularity: Notation and two-stage formulation precede feature extraction, MCE IRL, cost map and Hybrid A*.
papers.results_logic: Cost-function isolation → hardware/protocol → training/generalisation scenarios → supervision sensitivity → baselines.
papers.discussion_boundary: Risk–distance–time trade-off, metric applicability and comparator wins are explicit; OOD material/sensor limits are stated.
papers.figure_role: Scenario and route evidence are paired with five operational metrics and sensitivity results.
papers.citation_function: Demonstration, terrain-feature and navigation references each support one stage of the gap.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Held-out scenarios contain no new demonstrations; time is interpreted against a stated operational requirement.
papers.noncopy: MCE IRL, demonstrations, feature bins, Hybrid A*, scenarios, counts, hardware, numerical results and references.

papers.title: Subtask-masked curriculum learning for reinforcement learning with application to UAV maneuver decision-making
papers.introduction_move: Sparse reward/concurrent subtasks → curriculum limits → task/transfer masks.
papers.methods_granularity: RL/TD3/curriculum background precedes concepts, sequencing, transfer, distillation and pseudocode.
papers.results_logic: Question-led ablations → RL baselines → final-policy behaviour → expert comparison → limitations.
papers.discussion_boundary: Negative transfer and best-seed selection are disclosed; curve mechanisms are labelled as interpretations.
papers.figure_role: Ten-seed mean/SD curves, final metrics and state traces separate learning speed from final behaviour.
papers.citation_function: Hierarchical and curriculum references isolate the simultaneous-subtask and transfer gaps.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: Ten seeds support learning comparisons, but best-seed downstream evaluation limits population-level claims.
papers.noncopy: Military manoeuvre, curriculum/task/transfer masks, TD3, distillation, expert policy, seed selection, results and references.

papers.title: Multi-UAV trajectory optimizer: A sustainable system for wireless data harvesting with deep reinforcement learning
papers.introduction_move: Persistent wireless harvesting → centralized/resource-awareness limits → multi-agent system.
papers.methods_granularity: Environment, battery/charging and communication models precede Dec-POMDP, safety controller, reward, DDQN and transfer.
papers.results_logic: Settings/baselines → transfer effect → routes → parameter effects/trade-offs → larger-map experiments.
papers.discussion_boundary: Safety controller is distinct from learning; conflicting objectives and retrained larger environments are reported without universal generalisation.
papers.figure_role: Routes explain behaviour; Monte Carlo plots and tables support performance, sensitivity and scale claims.
papers.citation_function: Routing and MARL literature motivates decentralisation and resource-aware decisions.
papers.uncertainty_claim_strength: 99% CIs and 1000/300 Monte Carlo repetitions support simulation claims; post-hoc sweet spots remain exploratory.
papers.noncopy: Wireless model, Dec-POMDP, MARL/DDQN, charging thresholds, rewards, grids, ranges, sweet spots, results and references.

style_patterns.pattern: Move from an engineering constraint to a precise method/evidence gap and an explicit contribution list.
Define the task, state/action/resource constraints and evaluation semantics before presenting algorithmic detail or interpreting outcomes.
Disclose environment, parameters, baselines, metrics and computational setting before the main comparison.
Keep figures/tables close to the supported claim and assign different visual forms to architecture, learning, routes, metrics and ablations.
Report multiple engineering dimensions and preserve comparator wins, adverse costs or objective conflicts rather than declaring a universal champion.
State simulation, held-out, hardware and deployment boundaries explicitly; a more realistic tier supports only the claims tested in that tier.
Separate training conditions from evaluation or held-out conditions and state what changes or remains fixed.
Use named perturbations or scenario shifts and interpret robustness within those tested ranges.
Include a dedicated or clearly identifiable limitations/deployment-boundary discussion.
When physical validation is claimed, disclose platform/instrumentation, test protocol, sample counts or failures, and separate it from simulation.
style_patterns.use: Boundary rule only; current paper has no physical validation

style_patterns.pattern: Show replicated learning or evaluation uncertainty using seeds, repeated runs, intervals or dispersion.
style_patterns.use: Adopt because the frozen project supports it, not because it is universal

style_patterns.pattern: Use explicit component-removal or configuration ablations before making mechanism-specific claims.
style_patterns.use: Adopt for the four frozen ablations; do not infer untested submask effects

style_patterns.pattern: Provide a notation/nomenclature table for equation-dense sections.
Decompose online latency by planning/generation/control or internal module.
style_patterns.use: Use only where frozen timing data support the decomposition

style_patterns.pattern: Place Related work after the main empirical discussion.
